architecture: 84x84 x4 stack, cnn(32,64,64), 1-layer transformer d_model=64, linear head, 325,964 params
training: plain cross-entropy, 1,000 steps (0.82 epochs), batch 64, lr 3e-4
why_1000_steps: 1,000 is the best rung of the steps ladder in data/depth_vs_steps.json, but the margin is not resolvable: x_median 722.5 at 1,000 against 722.0 at 15,000, at n=100 on one training seed, and the artifact records monotone_decline_from_first_rung=false. It is the operating point this project uses, not an optimum the measurement can establish.
measurement_basis: single life from the 1-1 level start
how_these_were_made: 200 episodes were filmed live on one session and the takes matching each claim were kept; the rest were deleted. We do NOT reproduce a named episode from a stored trace -- see reproduction_note.
reproduction_note: A named episode cannot be re-filmed. session.reset() restores RAM byte-identically, but SMB's own pseudo-random state advances with total frames elapsed and is not cleared by a level restart, so an episode's outcome depends on the session's whole history. Measured on seed 99 of peak_PK32_84_s0_t0.7_200 (stored trace: x=3266): x=312 when run first on a fresh session, x=1537 after replaying episodes 0..98. Prefix replay gets closer and still does not reproduce, because the eval harness can resume an arm from a partial, making the original history unrecoverable. Block 58's determinism check passed because it compared repeats in the SAME position -- a different question. Consequence: these clips are honest footage of what the policy did on camera, not re-enactments of specific published episodes.

clips.caption: Level 1-1 completed from the level start. The policy reaches the flagpole and the game advances to World 1-2.
clips.verified: the clip's final frame shows the HUD reading WORLD 1-2 and Mario underground in the next level -- checked visually, not inferred from a distance number
clips.encoding: fps 10, width 320 (stepped down to stay under GitHub's ~10 MB inline limit)
clips.context: This happens on about 4 of 200 episodes. A fixed-rate script completes it 1 of 200 (Fisher p=0.372), so the completion is real and is NOT evidence of learned skill.

clips.caption: The policy past the Koopas at x=1248 -- the obstacle class where learning beats a representation-matched baseline.
clips.context: At the Koopas the policy beats a run-length script matched on its own token marginals by +5.5 pp, 10 of 10 paired seeds, p=0.0020 (the design floor), surviving Bonferroni. This is the project's one establishable positive result. The mechanism was specified in advance: the Koopas move, and screen-conditioning must pay where the obstacle moves.

not_filmed: An over-training comparison (1,000 vs 45,000 steps) was attempted and dropped: both snapshots died at the Goomba in the episodes filmed, so a side-by-side would have shown nothing. The loss/behaviour divergence is better shown as the numbers in data/depth_vs_steps.json than as footage.
